t: In front of you, in the garden of the National Gallery, is a bronze statue of James II. It shows him as a Roman emperor, in armour and a laurel wreath. It came from the workshop of Grinling Gibbons, though contemporary accounts suggest the Flemish sculptors Peter van Dievoet and Laurens van der Meulen did the work. It was first put up in 1686 at the old Palace of Whitehall, only two years before James was deposed, and has been moved several times since. Tobias Rustat, a courtier to Charles II, commissioned it.
